title: U.S. House · Georgia's 12th District
area: East Georgia, including Augusta, Columbia County, and Statesboro.

context.text: Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rate this race Solid Republican, Sabato's Crystal Ball rates it Safe Republican, and Decision Desk rates it Likely Republican.

candidates.name: Rick Allen

summary.text: Rick Allen is the Republican incumbent in Georgia's 12th District, which he has represented since 2015. A native of Augusta, he built a construction company over several decades before entering Congress, where he now chairs the House Committee on Education and Workforce. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

background.text: Born in Augusta, Georgia, in 1951; graduated from Evans High School in 1969.
Graduated from Auburn University in 1973 with a B.S. in building construction.

Worked as an estimator, project administrator, and assistant to the president at an Augusta construction firm before founding his own company, R. W. Allen & Associates, Inc., in 1976. His congressional biography says the company has operated in the Augusta and Athens communities for 50 years.

Received the Augusta Metro Chamber of Commerce Small Business Person of the Year award in 2008, took part in the first class of Leadership Augusta in 1980, and was inducted into the CSRA Business Hall of Fame in 2011, according to his House biography.
Ran for the Republican nomination for this seat in 2012 and lost the primary runoff to Lee Anderson.
Won the Republican primary on May 20, 2014, and defeated Democratic incumbent John Barrow in the November 4, 2014 general election; took office in 2015.
Served on the House Committee on Agriculture for eight years and sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee, according to his House biography.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Education and Workforce and as Vice Chair of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
According to his House biography, he and his wife, Robin, live in Augusta, have four children, and he is an active member of Trinity on the Hill Global Methodist Church.

priorities.text: Says a top focus is promoting economic policies that spur growth, create jobs, and reduce the size and scope of the federal government.
As a member of the House Agriculture Committee, says helping craft the farm bill and supporting agriculture producers is a priority for Georgia's 12th District.
As a senior member of the House Education and Workforce Committee, says he is working to keep K-12 education local while ensuring students are prepared to enter the workforce.

positions.summary: Introduced the Education Freedom Scholarships and Opportunity Act, which would create a federal tax credit for donations to nonprofit scholarship funds supporting elementary, secondary, and career and technical education.
positions.quote: That’s why I introduced the Education Freedom Scholarships and Opportunity Act alongside my House Education and Labor Committee colleague, Rep. Burgess Owens (UT-04). The bill expands quality elementary, secondary, and career and technical education opportunities for students by providing a federal tax credit to encourage individuals and businesses to donate to nonprofit scholarship funds.

record.text: Serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Education and Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), and also sits on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Sponsored the Better Agriculture Resources Now (BARN) Act, which would move administration of the H-2A agricultural visa program from the Department of Labor to the Department of Agriculture.

Introduced the Education Freedom Scholarships and Opportunity Act with Rep. Burgess Owens (UT-04), creating a federal tax credit for donations to nonprofit K-12 and career/technical education scholarship funds.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and record above are drawn from Allen's official House issues pages (Economy & Jobs, Agriculture, Education), which describe 2017-2018 legislative activity still posted as his current issue statements; no newer statements on these topics were found on his official site.

candidates.name: Ceretta Smith
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16 Democratic primary runoff over Traci George, 55.8%

summary.text: Ceretta Smith is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 12th District, having won the June 16 primary runoff. A U.S. Army veteran who served as a medic, she worked 25 years as a federal employee and rose to leadership in the American Federation of Government Employees, and has served on the Grovetown city council. She ran for the Georgia State Senate in 2020 and describes her campaign as focused on restoring trust in government and economic opportunity.

background.text: Born in Fayetteville, North Carolina, in 1968; graduated from Fayetteville Terry Sanford High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the Minnesota Graduate School of Theology in 2004, a graduate degree from the Calvary Bible Institute in 2008, and a degree from Deeper Bible College in 2024.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1992 to 2000, nearly a decade by her own account, as a medic stationed in Germany.
Worked 25 years as a federal employee, including as a physical evaluation boards liaison officer at Dwight David Eisenhower Army Medical Center, and also worked as a substitute teacher.

Rose through the American Federation of Government Employees as Women's and Fair Practices Coordinator, Chief Steward, Legislative Political Coordinator, Local President, Georgia State Council President, and National Fair Practices Coordinator.
Ran for Georgia State Senate District 23 in 2020 as a Democrat and lost to Republican Max Burns in the general election.
First elected to the Grovetown city council in 2021; describes a citywide literacy initiative that distributed books to children.
Announced her campaign for Georgia's 12th District in 2025 and won the Democratic primary runoff on June 16, 2026.
Says she has lived in Grovetown for 20 years with her husband, a retired Army sergeant first class.

priorities.text: Says she is running "to restore trust in government by putting people before party" and will "work across the aisle."
Campaign centers on economic opportunity: creating jobs, lowering costs, supporting small businesses and family farmers, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
Says she will work to improve access to affordable healthcare and education and to ensure veterans and rural communities get needed resources.

positions.summary: Says she will work to improve access to affordable healthcare.
